sections.h2: Who records deeds and mortgages in Nash County?
sections.html:
The Nash County Register of Deeds records real estate documents for every parcel that lies inside Nash County. The county's own page says the office holds real estate records back to 1777, marriage records from 1862, and birth and death records from October 1913.

Deeds from 1777 through 1969 can be searched online. Newer land records are available as hard copies, so a seller who needs a prior deed, a plat or an old deed of trust should ask the office directly at (252) 459-9836, the number printed on the county's filing standards page.

sections.h2: Which county records a house in Rocky Mount?
sections.html:
The county where the land sits does the recording, and for Rocky Mount that can be Nash or Edgecombe. The county's own health report notes that Rocky Mount lies in both counties, while the rest of Nash County is mostly rural.

Before anyone drafts a deed for a Rocky Mount address, check which county's tax parcel record covers the lot. A deed sent to the wrong office will not give the buyer protection against later claims. For a parcel that spans two or more counties, G.S. 105-228.30 sends the excise tax to the county that holds the greater share of the value.

Nash County was formed in 1777 from the western part of Edgecombe County. It shares borders with Edgecombe, Wilson, Johnston, Franklin and Halifax Counties, and the county's health report lists eleven municipalities:

  • County seat: Nashville
  • Eastern area: Rocky Mount and Sharpsburg
  • Northern area: Dortches, Castalia, Red Oak and Whitakers
  • Southern area: Middlesex and Bailey
  • Western area: Momeyer and Spring Hope

sections.h2: What must a deed look like before Nash County will record it?
sections.html:
It must meet the paper standards in G.S. 161-14(b), which the county summarizes on its filing standards page. A deed that misses them can still be recorded, but the office collects a $25.00 nonstandard document fee.

The county lists these points for instruments recorded on or after July 1, 2002:

  • Paper that is 8 1/2 by 11 inches or 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • A blank 3 inch margin at the top of the first page.
  • Black type on white paper, with a font no smaller than 10 points.
  • Text on one side of each page only.
  • The type of instrument written at the top of the first page, below the blank margin.

The county adds that blanks may be filled in with a pen and that corrections may be made in pen. The page also says the side margins changed from one half inch to one quarter inch effective October 1, 2011. If the font falls under 10 points but the Register judges the text legible, the office may skip the nonstandard fee.

sections.h2: What does recording cost at the Nash County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Recording fees are set statewide, so Nash County charges the same amounts as any other North Carolina county. For a general instrument the fee is $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each page after that, and the statute calls these fees complete and exclusive.

Statewide recording fees under G.S. 161-10, collected by the Nash County Register of Deeds
DocumentFee as printed in the statute
General instrument such as a deed$26.00 for the first 15 pages, plus $4.00 each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for the first 35 pages, plus $4.00 each added page
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, plus $2.00 each added page
Nonstandard document add-on$25.00

Source: G.S. 161-10. Fees are collected before the document is filed, and the same statute lists $10.00 for each additional instrument included in one document.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Nash County house sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays it. G.S. 105-228.30 says the transferor must pay the tax to the register of deeds of the county where the property sits, before the deed is recorded.

The rate is $1.00 on each $500.00 of consideration or value, or any fraction of $500.00 left over. Half of the collection stays with the county general fund. The other half, less refunds and an allowance, goes to the Department of Revenue each month, and the county may keep 2% of the State share.

For a Nash County seller this tax is a closing cost on the settlement statement, separate from income tax. The Register of Deeds only collects it and affixes the stamp, so questions about what a house sold for are answered by the stamp amount on the recorded deed.

sections.h2: Can a Nash County deed be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The county accepts e-recording for real estate, and a filer first has to register by signing a Memorandum of Understanding with the Register of Deeds office.

After the office receives the MOU it issues a number to use when filing. The county says recordings are received from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, Monday through Friday, except holidays.

sections.h2: Why does recording matter when you sell a house in Nash County?
sections.html:
Recording fixes the buyer's place in line. Under G.S. 47-18 a conveyance, an option, a lease over three years, a right of first refusal or a right of first offer does not bind lien creditors or later purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the order and time of registration.

That rule is the reason unrecorded paperwork causes trouble. Typical examples sellers run into:

  • A deed signed years ago by a parent but never recorded.
  • A paid-off loan whose cancellation was never filed.
  • A contract for deed that was never recorded or memorialized.

Cancellations of a deed of trust carry no recording fee, so clearing an old loan costs little. If the lender cannot be found, ask a North Carolina attorney how to proceed. Staff at the register's office cannot give legal advice.

sections.h2: What do Nash County housing figures look like for sellers?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 99,365 residents in Nash County as of July 1, 2025, up 4.6% from the April 2020 base, spread over 540.44 square miles of land. Housing units numbered 45,068, and the owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024 was 63.6%.

For the same period the median value of an owner-occupied home was $191,000, median gross rent was $953 a month, and median household income was $62,426. The county issued 483 building permits in 2025, and 21.7% of residents were 65 or older. Those older owners are often the ones facing inherited property, a deed that needs correcting, or a house that needs more work than they want to take on.

A cash sale does not skip the recording step. The deed still goes to the register's office, and the excise tax still applies.

sections.h2: What should a Nash County seller bring to the recording step?
sections.html:
Bring the documents the closing attorney asked for, plus any paperwork that clears a title problem. In Nash County that usually comes down to a short list.

  • The signed, acknowledged deed, printed to the paper standards above.
  • The funds for the recording fee and the excise tax, which the seller owes before recording.
  • Any cancellation of an old deed of trust, which records without a fee.
  • A plat, if the lot was divided, at $21.00 per sheet.

If a prior owner died without a recorded deed, the estate has to be handled through the Clerk of Superior Court of the county where the person lived. Ask that clerk what is needed before a buyer can take title.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Nash County property?
faqs.a: Record it with the Nash County Register of Deeds, unless the lot is in the Edgecombe County portion of Rocky Mount. Call (252) 459-9836 to confirm filing details before you send anything.

faqs.q: How much does the Nash County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: A general instrument costs $26.00 for up to 15 pages plus $4.00 for each added page, under G.S. 161-10. A deed that fails the paper standards also pays a $25.00 nonstandard fee.
Yes, after the filer signs a Memorandum of Understanding with the Register of Deeds and receives a filing number. The county lists receipt hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays except holidays.

faqs.q: Who pays the Nash County deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller does. The statute puts the duty on the transferor and sets the rate at $1.00 for each $500.00 of value, paid to the register before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Nash County house if the deed was never recorded?
faqs.a: Usually yes, but the gap has to be fixed first, because an unrecorded conveyance does not bind later buyers or lien creditors. Ask a North Carolina attorney to prepare and record the missing deed before closing.
